mutants.rationale: Read the single C4 witness (1,0,1,0)->(2,0,0,0) as "the" minimizer; the minimizer set is a simplex with 10 points.
The source orbit SUM (1,1,1,1) has total 4 while Phi1 = 2; the canonical symmetric point is the orbit average (1/2 each).
Round the symmetric selector 1/6 to an integer cochain; the cyclically invariant minimizer is integral only when n divides the holonomy.
Accept holonomy 0 as a valid weight vector; the minimizer is the zero residual and the declared total M = 0 is refused.
Claim non-uniqueness for a 1-cycle; the class has a single point there, so the hypothesis n >= 2 cannot be dropped.
Claim the weight of a single sector (all edges) varies; it equals Phi1 for every minimizer, so only a split into two or more sectors is undetermined.
Phi1 is the minimum of the L1 form over the class c - d0 h, not the raw L1 form of the representative c (off by the gauge).
For holonomy -3 the minimizers are the nonpositive cochains; sign convention swapped.
Gamma2 is the signed holonomy; replacing it by |S| loses the orientation of the class.
Count minimizers by their distinct sector-weight vectors (3) instead of by residual cochains (10).
With unequal declared edge masses (1,2,3,4) the minimizer is the single point (2,0,0,0) on the minimal-mass edge; the equal-mass non-uniqueness table does not carry over.
If Gamma2 were the sum of squares of the weights it is 2 for (1,1,0,0) but 4 for (2,0,0,0): the minimizers do not share it, so the two readings of Gamma2 give different fibers.
For two disjoint cycles with holonomies 2 and -1 the total holonomy is 1 but Phi1 = 3; one holonomy no longer determines the class or Phi1.
With masses (2,2,1,1) both minimal edges lie in the second sector, so the sector weights (0,3) are determined although the minimizer is not unique.
